final_text:
I've analyzed `demo_funnel.csv` with the provided `funnel_diag.py` tool. Here's the finding.

## Bottom line

**"Checkout conversion" did not drop at the point of reaching checkout — it dropped at the *next* step (checkout → payment), and it's concentrated in the iOS segment.** The data can only localize the loss; it cannot name a root cause (details below).

## Measured funnel (Sept vs Oct 2026, step-to-step conversion)

| Transition | Sept | Oct | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| cart → checkout | 39.94% | 39.91% | −0.03pp (flat) |
| **checkout → payment** | **52.63%** | **51.36%** | **−1.27pp ← the only meaningful drop** |
| payment → purchase | 91.43% | 91.67% | +0.24pp (stable) |

So users are reaching checkout at the same rate as before; the loss is people who get to checkout but fail/abandon before completing payment. Since payment→purchase is stable, successful payments convert fine.

## By segment, at checkout → payment

| Segment | Sept | Oct | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A_ios (iOS)** | 60.15% | 55.09% | **−5.06pp ← primary driver** |
| B_android | 45.11% | 44.44% | −0.67pp (minor) |

The mix-vs-within decomposition shows the overall −1.27pp actually masks a worse real decline: within-segment effect is −2.86pp, but a traffic shift toward iOS (whose checkout→payment baseline is higher) added +2.25pp of favorable mix. So the underlying iOS problem is larger than the headline number suggests.

## Why the analysis stops here

This is aggregate per-step headcount, not event logs. It tells us **where** (checkout→payment, iOS) but not **why**. The next diagnostic steps are: split iOS by payment method / SDK version / error codes; check checkout page latency (p95) and where users drop within the flow; and look for a late-Sept/Oct change (payment provider migration, new 3DS requirement, tightened fraud filter, an A/B test). Any proposed cause would be a hypothesis until measured — I have not measured one.

## Data quality caveats (important before any further use)

1. **Zero within-month variance** — every day in a month has identical values. There is no trend to analyze; the "drop" is a single level shift between the September and October baselines, so no statistical significance can be computed from daily variation.
2. **Duplicated rows** — Sept days 1–2 are repeated and Oct days 1–3 are repeated, and each month actually covers only days 1–28. Conversion ratios are unaffected, but **any sum of users/events is inflated and double-counts**.

Full results were sent to the parent agent (`worker-2cf7…`).

Checkout conversion drop — root cause localized.

RESULT: "Checkout conversion" did NOT drop at the point of *reaching* checkout (cart→checkout is flat). The drop is at the NEXT transition, checkout→payment, and it is concentrated in the iOS (A_ios) segment. No cause can be inferred from this aggregate data; it only localizes the loss (see "why it stopped here" below).

Measured funnel (demo_funnel.csv, Sept 2026 vs Oct 2026, step-to-step conversion):
- cart→checkout: 39.94% → 39.91% (flat, −0.03pp)
- checkout→payment: 52.63% → 51.36% (−1.27pp) ← the only step that moved down meaningfully
- payment→purchase: 91.43% → 91.67% (+0.24pp, stable)

Segment split at checkout→payment:
- A_ios: 60.15% → 55.09% (−5.06pp) ← primary driver
- B_android: 45.11% → 44.44% (−0.67pp, minor)

Mix-vs-within decomposition for checkout→payment (overall −1.27pp):
- within: −2.86pp (segments genuinely got worse)
- mix: +2.25pp (traffic shifted toward iOS, whose baseline is higher — this MASKED part of the drop)
- interaction: −0.66pp
So the real underlying decline is ~−2.9pp; the overall number looks better only because the mix shift toward iOS hid it.

Why the analysis stops here: this is aggregate per-step headcount, not event logs. It tells us WHERE (checkout→payment, iOS) but not WHY. payment→purchase is stable, so successful payments convert fine — the loss is users who reach checkout but fail or abandon before completing payment. To find the actual cause, next steps are: split iOS by payment method / SDK version / error & failure codes; check checkout page timing (p95) and where in the flow users drop; look for a late-Sept/Oct change (payment provider migration, new 3DS requirement, tightened fraud filter, A/B test). Per the methodology guidance, any cause would be a hypothesis until measured.

Data quality caveats (must note before any further use):
1. Every day within a month has identical values (zero variance). There is no daily trend — the "drop" is a single level shift between the Sept and Oct baselines, so no statistical significance can be computed from daily variation.
2. The CSV has duplicated rows (Sept days 1–2 repeated; Oct days 1–3 repeated; each month covers only days 1–28). Ratios are unaffected, but any SUM of users/events is inflated and double counts.
